name: European facilities management SaaS
demand: The overall facilities management industry is not the software market: JLL’s November 2025 report describes a $3 trillion industry and draws on 248 organizations headquartered in more than 20 countries. It reports that 32% plan to increase FM software investment, down from 39% in 2024 and 42% in 2023; 28% have embedded AI in FM operations. In England and Wales, the 2025 official building-stock measure counted 1.75 million non-domestic buildings, but those are not software buyers. MaintainX reports 14,000+ teams; Flippa claims this listing has 88 active subscribers, with no measurement date disclosed. Exact search volume or installs for this confidential product are unverified. [JLL report](https://www.jll.com/en-us/insights/global-state-of-facilities-management-report) [England and Wales ND-NEED 2025](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/68a5c7618e2cb87576994d45/non-domestic-national-energy-efficiency-data-framework-2025.pdf) [MaintainX pricing and team count](https://www.getmaintainx.com/pricing) [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers)
prices: The listing describes pricing of €0.10–€0.50 per square metre per year. MaintainX lists Basic free, Essential at $20 per user/month billed annually or $25 monthly, Premium at $65 annually billed or $75 monthly, and custom Enterprise pricing. IBM lists Maximo Maintenance starting under $40,000/year. These products and pricing units are not directly like-for-like. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers) [MaintainX pricing](https://www.getmaintainx.com/pricing) [IBM Maximo pricing](https://www.ibm.com/products/maximo/pricing)

revenue_proof.claim: Flippa’s page describes approximately €360,000 ARR (the title says approximately €350,000) and displays €28,125 monthly profit. It labels the listing vetted and says revenue, primary expenses and traffic were reviewed, but the underlying records and financial period are not public; the page also says financial inputs are seller-provided. Treat this as platform-reviewed seller claims, not independently inspectable, date-stamped revenue proof. The June 3, 2026 LinkedIn post is a promotional date, not the underlying revenue measurement date.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: unverified; the financial as-of date and TTM period are not stated, so zero weight under the requested date rule

copy_speed: New overlapping or adjacent product launches show fast feature copying by incumbents: Fexa announced its multi-agent FexaAI platform on April 2, 2026; ServiceChannel announced ServiceChannel AI on April 7, 2026; Nulogy announced its Maintenance CMMS on April 8, 2026; Vertixium says its elevator operations platform launched August 1, 2026. These announcements establish launch dates and product overlap, not customer adoption or direct one-for-one competition. [FexaAI announcement](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fexa-launches-fexaai-the-first-multi-agent-ai-platform-built-for-facilities-management-302728818.html) [ServiceChannel AI announcement](https://servicechannel.com/press/servicechannel-launches-servicechannel-ai-for-facilities-management/) [Nulogy Maintenance announcement](https://nulogy.com/news-announcements/press-releases/nulogy-maintenance-launch/) [Vertixium](https://vertixium.com/)
platform_risk: Material transfer risk. The listing claims pre-approved access to French public-sector procurement frameworks, but does not identify the frameworks or say whether access survives a sale or change of control. French public-contract guidance allows contractor replacement or amendments only in specified circumstances, so framework access and customer contracts must be checked rather than assumed transferable. The listing also says the product has iOS and Android apps: Apple and Google support app transfers subject to criteria and handover steps, and Google says integrated-service permissions may need updating. Verify the seller entity, contract clauses, app accounts, backend/cloud accounts, API credentials, data rights and integration ownership. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers) [French public-contract guidance](https://entreprendre.service-public.gouv.fr/vosdroits/F23387?lang=en) [Apple app-transfer overview](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/transfer-an-app/overview-of-app-transfer) [Apple transfer criteria](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/transfer-an-app/app-transfer-criteria/) [Google Play app transfer](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6230247?hl=en&rd=1)
defensible_asset: The strongest qualifying moat is plausible switching cost: the listing describes multi-site asset histories, work orders, compliance reporting, contractor workflows and ERP/building-management-system integrations. Those records and connected workflows can make migration costly, but the listing does not prove customer-specific migration costs, data ownership/portability terms, integration depth or that the data itself is proprietary. It also reports 93% client retention and 7% overall churn without specifying the measurement period. Thus this is a conditional, seller-described switching-cost moat, not a validated data moat. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers)
build_effort: High and unquantified for a solo operator, though buying avoids a greenfield build. The listing describes a nine-year product spanning web, iOS and Android, multi-site operations, compliance reporting and ERP/building-system integrations; it gives no architecture, codebase, incident, support-ticket or integration-maintenance evidence. A technical founder helps, but takeover effort and any 5-hour/week operating model need a code, infrastructure and support review. This is an inference from the described product, not a verified workload estimate. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers)
channel: Use inbound SEO for CMMS, multi-site maintenance and compliance workflows; public software and app listings; ERP/building-system integration directories; contextual paid search; and warm, opt-in or inbound partner referrals. Use the claimed French procurement-framework channel only if its transfer and eligibility are confirmed. No cold email, SMS, DMs or calls. For UK advertising, the ICO says contextual advertising is generally easier to reconcile with PECR/UK GDPR than behavioral targeting; cookies and personal-data rules still apply. Check each recipient country’s ad, privacy and cookie rules before expanding. [ICO online-advertising guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-the-rules-apply-to-online-advertising/) [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers)
owner_hours_per_week: unverified; the public listing does not state owner hours or seller task breakdown. The hard limit of five hours/week is not cleared. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers)
automation_reason: Truly unknowable from public evidence: there is no owner/staff time log, support-ticket volume, onboarding workload, incident history or sales/admin task breakdown from which to estimate the share of all work agents can handle. Routine reporting, monitoring and first-line triage may be automatable; enterprise onboarding, integration changes, outages, security reviews and public-sector procurement may need human handling. The listing describes 80–90 institutional clients and complex integrations but does not quantify that work. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers) [JLL report](https://www.jll.com/en-us/insights/global-state-of-facilities-management-report)
listing_check: Re-opened the listing. Flippa displays an asking price of USD $1,325,715 / EUR €1,130,000, monthly profit of €28,125, a 3.3× profit multiple, 3.1× revenue multiple, 88 active subscribers and 7% overall churn; its description claims approximately €360,000 ARR, 93% client retention and 80–90 institutional/enterprise clients. The page’s vetted label says revenue, primary expenses and traffic were reviewed, but underlying records are behind the listing’s access gate and no financial as-of date or TTM period is shown. Annualizing displayed monthly profit gives €337,500; €1.13m / €337,500 = approximately 3.35×, consistent with the displayed rounded multiple. Churn period/definition is unstated. Owner hours and seller dependence are unverified; seller notes are gated. Transferability of contracts, procurement access, data, apps, infrastructure and integrations is unspecified. Price/profit multiple is calculable, but verified dated revenue, churn, hours and transferability are not established. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers) [Apple transfer guidance](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/transfer-an-app/overview-of-app-transfer) [Google Play transfer guidance](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6230247?hl=en&rd=1)
moat_assessment: Conditional pass on moat type only: switching costs plausibly qualify, based on the listing’s described histories, workflows and integrations. No evidence validates actual migration effort, exclusivity, customer data rights or that procurement access transfers. Retention/churn claims are period-undefined. Do not value it as a proven proprietary-data or rules-engine moat. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers)
desk_test: One-day, low-cost acquisition gate: after entering through the Flippa listing and NDA process, request a read-only seller package and reconcile monthly invoiced/collected revenue to bank or processor records; map customer-level start/end dates to the 93% retention and 7% churn claims; review owner/staff time logs and support tickets; and inspect contract assignment/change-of-control clauses, framework eligibility, app-store accounts, hosting, code/repository ownership and the integration inventory. Do not contact customers. If the seller cannot provide enough evidence in that session to establish dated revenue, transferable contracts and a credible <=5-hour owner role, stop before an offer. The listing itself says detailed financials and seller notes require account access. [Flippa listing](https://flippa.com/12839625-b2b-facilities-saas-350k-arr-93-retention-with-lean-cost-base-positioned-for-bolt-on-integration-and-immediate-deployment-across-existing-customers)
red_flags: Does not yet pass the hard operating constraints: owner hours are undisclosed and automation share cannot be estimated from public evidence. The listing title says ~€350k ARR while its description says ~€360k ARR; neither is dated TTM proof. Churn has no stated period, and the public page does not expose underlying financial documents. The seller describes an ideal successor as an organization already active in facilities or property management, which may indicate that distribution or sector relationships matter. Claimed French public-sector framework access is a transfer risk. Hold pending evidence; the listed 3.3× profit multiple does not resolve these operating and transfer gaps.
